newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed mixed with longer maturities pulled higher by German Bunds and shorter paper weakened by talk of a hike in Dutch term interest rates.
But dealers detected little response to the widely expected tightening of monetary policy with the losses in the short end of the guilder curve incurred in expectation of the move.

Dutch bonds had markedly underperformed their German equivalents ahead of the central bank's action. It lifted the secured loans rate, equivalent to Germany's discount rate, by 50 basis points to 2.50 percent and the special advances rate, like the repo rate, by 20 basis points to 2.90 percent.
"It was anticipated, so not too much happened," said one trader.
Dealers said the possibility of another hike would depend on whether the guilder continued to weaken against the mark.
The Dutch currency strengthened slightly after the central bank announcement.

"The central bank will not hesitate to increase rates even more, above German rates (if the guilder weakens)," said the trader. Germany's repo rate is 10 basis points higher than in the Netherlands, although German inflation is lower, but the discount rate is now the same.
"The reaction in the bond market has been pretty muted," said another dealer, adding that most players had squared their positions ahead of the 1500 GMT rate hike announcement.
He said that with Dutch base rates in line with Germany, all that remained to be done was to raise the special advances rate by 10 basis points.
He also noted a slight steepening of the guilder yield curve after the move as the pressure on shorter paper eased.
Most of the gains at the long end of the Dutch market were registered at the opening as guilder paper tracked the direction of Bunds, in turn strengthened by Treasuries on Friday.
